text: Where is the class decorator that generates dunder methods for attribute-heavy classes defined in attrs?
rationale: src/attr/_make.py:1325 defines attrs ('A class decorator that adds dunder methods according to the specified attributes'); its inner closure wrap (_make.py:1441) applies the transformation to each decorated class, and attr/__init__.py re-exports it (with the aliases s / attributes at __init__.py:32).

text: Where is attrib defined, the legacy helper that declares a single field on a class?
rationale: src/attr/_make.py:106 defines attrib ('Create a new field / attribute on a class'), normalizing factory/default sugar and wrapping validator+converter lists before returning a _CountingAttr; attr/__init__.py:33 aliases it as attr and ib.

text: Where is the Attribute class defined, the immutable runtime representation of a field?
rationale: src/attr/_make.py:2429 declares the slotted, frozen Attribute class; from_counting_attr (_make.py:2562) converts the declarative _CountingAttr form into it during class building.

text: Where is the intermediate attribute representation that keeps a global counter to preserve definition order?
rationale: src/attr/_make.py:2696 defines _CountingAttr, the internal structure whose cls_counter orders fields authored before the decorator runs; attrib returns one (_make.py:196) and _transform_attrs converts them into Attributes.

text: Where is Factory defined, the wrapper that turns a callable into a per-instance default?
rationale: src/attr/_make.py:3029 defines Factory (slots factory/takes_self, pickling via __getstate__/__setstate__ at 3054/3060); attrib wraps factory= arguments in one (_make.py:181) and _CountingAttr.default builds one for decorator-set defaults (_make.py:2839).

text: Where is the Converter class defined, the wrapper that lets a converter receive the instance and the field?
rationale: src/attr/_make.py:3087 defines Converter, which stores takes_self/takes_field and builds the matching __call__ lambda (3126-3136); optional (converters.py:61) and pipe (_make.py:3405) both return instances of it.

text: Where is the helper that builds a whole attrs class from a name and a list of attribute names defined?
rationale: src/attr/_make.py:3206 defines make_class, which packs the names/dict into a class body, applies _determine_attrs_eq_order for proper warnings, and delegates to attrs with these= (_make.py:3301); the hypothesis strategies and dozens of tests call it.

text: Where is the function that creates a new instance from an existing one with keyword changes applied?
rationale: src/attr/_make.py:587 defines evolve: it reads the class's fields, fills each init-taking field's init alias from the current instance when not overridden (_make.py:634-640), and calls cls(**changes); the builder also attaches it as __replace__ (add_replace, _make.py:1106).

text: Where is fields defined, the accessor that returns a class's attribute tuple with name access?
rationale: src/attr/_make.py:1891 defines fields: it accepts a class or instance (26.1.0), resolves generic aliases through get_generic_base, caches __attrs_attrs__, and raises NotAnAttrsClassError otherwise; asdict/astuple/assoc/resolve_types/evolve/validate all consume it.

text: Where is the sentinel enum used when None is ambiguous as a default value defined?
rationale: src/attr/_make.py:62 defines the _Nothing enum whose single NOTHING variant reprs as 'NOTHING' (__repr__, 75) and is falsy (__bool__, 78); the module-level NOTHING constant is assigned at _make.py:82.

text: Where is the recursive serializer that turns an attrs instance into a nested dictionary defined?
rationale: src/attr/_funcs.py:28 defines asdict (recurse/filter/dict_factory/retain_collection_types/value_serializer); the anything-recursive helper _asdict_anything (_funcs.py:154) handles dict/collection elements that are not field values.

text: Where is the tuple counterpart of asdict defined?
rationale: src/attr/_funcs.py:232 defines astuple, mirroring asdict's recursion for tuple_factory-based output, including the namedtuple TypeError workaround at _funcs.py:311-318.

text: Where is the predicate that checks whether a class was decorated with attrs defined?
rationale: src/attr/_funcs.py:354 defines has: it probes __attrs_attrs__, then falls back to get_generic_base for specialized generics (A[str]) and caches the result on the class.

text: Where is assoc defined, the deprecated copy-with-changes helper?
rationale: src/attr/_funcs.py:382 defines assoc: copy.copy(inst), then _OBJ_SETATTR applies each change, raising AttrsAttributeNotFoundError for unknown names (_funcs.py:417-420); the docstring points to evolve as the replacement.

text: Where is the utility that resolves string and forward-reference annotations on attrs classes defined?
rationale: src/attr/_funcs.py:425 defines resolve_types: it caches via __attrs_types_resolved__, calls typing.get_type_hints with globalns/localns/include_extras, and _OBJ_SETATTRs the resolved type onto each frozen Attribute (_funcs.py:491).

text: Where is the factory that creates a comparison class with custom eq/order callables defined?
rationale: src/attr/_cmp.py:13 defines cmp_using: it assembles a slotted class body whose __eq__/__lt__/... come from _make_operator (_cmp.py:126), appends _check_same_type when require_same_type, and applies functools.total_ordering when 1-3 ordering functions are given.

text: Where is define defined, the modern keyword-only class decorator with slotted defaults?
rationale: src/attr/_next_gen.py:23 defines define (slots=True, auto_detect=True, auto_exc=True defaults); its wrap closure dispatches to do_it with the derived options, and attr/__init__.py re-exports it beside frozen/mutable.

text: Where is the next-generation field declaration function that forwards everything to the legacy one?
rationale: src/attr/_next_gen.py:437 defines field, a keyword-only wrapper that simply calls attrib with the same arguments (_next_gen.py:605); it is what attrs.field resolves to.

text: Where does the next-generation API define its own asdict variant that keeps collection types?
rationale: src/attr/_next_gen.py:623 defines asdict, a thin wrapper over _funcs.asdict that fixes retain_collection_types=True and dict as the dict_factory; the astuple twin sits at _next_gen.py:639.

text: Where is the version object that compares against 1-4 length tuples defined?
rationale: src/attr/_version_info.py:12 defines VersionInfo (an attrs class itself, total_ordering at line 10): _from_version_string (39) parses dotted strings, _ensure_tuple (51) normalizes comparisons, and __eq__/__lt__/__hash__ (70/78/88) implement the semantics.

text: Where is the converter that maps strings like yes, on and 1 to real booleans defined?
rationale: src/attr/converters.py:125 defines to_bool: it lowercases strings, matches the True/False value tables at converters.py:156-158, and raises ValueError for anything else.

text: Where is the converter factory that lets a field accept None in addition to the wrapped type?
rationale: src/attr/converters.py:21 defines optional: it branches on Converter instances (takes_self/takes_field call shape) and copies the wrapped converter's annotations via _AnnotationExtractor (converters.py:50-58).

text: Where is default_if_none defined, the converter that substitutes a fallback for None values?
rationale: src/attr/converters.py:66 defines default_if_none: exactly one of default/factory must be given (TypeErrors at 92-98), Factory takes_self is rejected (ValueError at 104-106), and the returned closure returns default or default.factory() when fed None.

text: Where is the asdict/astuple filter factory that keeps only the listed classes, names or attributes defined?
rationale: src/attr/filters.py:21 defines include: _split_what (filters.py:10) splits its arguments into class/name/Attribute frozensets and the returned include_ closure (38) keeps whatever matches any bucket.

text: Where is the inverse filter that drops the listed classes, names or attributes defined?
rationale: src/attr/filters.py:48 defines exclude, building on the same _split_what split as include but negating the membership test in the exclude_ closure (65).

text: Where is the on_setattr hook that chains multiple setters and returns the last value defined?
rationale: src/attr/setters.py:11 defines pipe, whose wrapped_pipe closure (18) folds each setter over the incoming value; a list/tuple on_setattr is auto-wrapped by attrib (_make.py:188) and attrs (_make.py:1439).

text: Where is the on_setattr hook that makes any attribute assignment fail defined?
rationale: src/attr/setters.py:29 defines frozen, which unconditionally raises FrozenAttributeError (imported from attr.exceptions at setters.py:8); NO_OP, the sentinel for per-attribute opt-out, sits at setters.py:79.

text: Where are the module-level toggles that turn validator execution on and off defined?
rationale: src/attr/_config.py:8 defines set_run_validators (TypeError for non-bool, mutates the module global _run_validators) and _config.py:23 defines get_run_validators returning it; validators.set_disabled/get_disabled (validators.py:57/69) are the non-deprecated front door onto them.

text: Where is the validator factory that checks values are instances of given types defined?
rationale: src/attr/validators.py:113 defines instance_of, building an _InstanceOfValidator (93) whose __call__ does the isinstance test and whose __repr__ names the tuple of types; not_ composes its output at validators.py:646.

text: Where is the validator that validates every member of an iterable, plus optionally the iterable itself, defined?
rationale: src/attr/validators.py:361 defines deep_iterable: it wraps the member validator (is_callable-checked) and optional iterable validator in an _DeepIterable (333) whose __call__ loops the members.

text: Where is the error raised when assigning to an attribute of a frozen class defined?
rationale: src/attr/exceptions.py:23 defines FrozenInstanceError, subclassing FrozenError (exceptions.py:6, an AttributeError mirroring namedtuples with the 'can't set attribute' message); the builder's generated __setattr__/_frozen_setattrs raise it (_make.py:573).

text: Where is the exception raised when a helpers function receives a class that attrs never decorated defined?
rationale: src/attr/exceptions.py:47 defines NotAnAttrsClassError (a ValueError); fields and fields_dict raise it when __attrs_attrs__ is absent (_make.py:1936/1967).

rationale: The only production caller is _ClassBuilder.__init__ (src/attr/_make.py:682); the direct unit coverage lives in tests/test_make.py (test_no_modifications 186, test_normal 195, test_empty 210, test_transforms_to_attribute 219, test_conflicting_defaults 238, test_kw_only 268, test_these 310).

text: Who calls fields to read a class's attribute tuple?
rationale: Five src callers: asdict (src/attr/_funcs.py:80), astuple (_funcs.py:274), assoc (_funcs.py:415), resolve_types (_funcs.py:488) in _funcs.py, plus evolve (src/attr/_make.py:633) and validate (_make.py:1983).

rationale: Five precise call sites, all in tests/test_funcs.py: test_empty (596), test_no_changes (607), test_change (624), test_unknown (637) and test_frozen (651).

rationale: 63 precise call sites; the hypothesis plumbing leads (tests/strategies.py:_create_hyp_nested_strategy at 71 and simple_classes at 200, tests/utils.py:simple_class at 24), followed by the dedicated suite in tests/test_make.py (test_simple 1358, test_dict 1371, test_catches_wrong_attrs_type 1437 and ~50 more).

text: Which library code calls attrib to declare fields?
rationale: _src callers: _transform_attrs wraps annotation values in one (src/attr/_make.py:417), make_class builds dict-based fields through it (_make.py:3259), _AndValidator declares its _validators slot (_make.py:3319), the next-gen field forwards to it (src/attr/_next_gen.py:605) and VersionInfo's four fields use it (src/attr/_version_info.py:33-35).

text: Who constructs Factory instances for defaults?
rationale: Three src constructors: attrib wraps factory= sugar (src/attr/_make.py:181), _CountingAttr.default builds takes_self factories for decorator-set defaults (_make.py:2839), and default_if_none wraps its factory= argument (src/attr/converters.py:101).

text: Who instantiates Converter to wrap converter callables?
rationale: Three src sites: _attrs_to_init_script registers per-field converter globals with it (src/attr/_make.py:2215), pipe returns it when any stage is a Converter (_make.py:3405), and optional preserves the instance/field call shape (src/attr/converters.py:61).

text: Who calls _collect_base_attrs to gather inherited fields?
rationale: Exactly one precise caller: _transform_attrs selects it for the collect_by_mro branch (src/attr/_make.py:452); the legacy misordering twin _collect_base_attrs_broken is selected at the adjacent else (456).

text: Which code paths call _make_init_script to generate __init__ source?
rationale: The two builder methods call it: add_init (src/attr/_make.py:1082) for __init__ and add_attrs_init (_make.py:1118) for __attrs_init__; the test helper _add_init re-implements the call shape in tests/test_dunders.py:89.

text: Who calls _attrs_to_init_script, the source emitter for init methods?
rationale: Exactly one precise caller: _make_init_script delegates every field/default/converter decision to it (src/attr/_make.py:2038).

text: Which function consults _determine_setters to pick how init assigns attributes?
rationale: Exactly _attrs_to_init_script (src/attr/_make.py:2184) — it receives the frozen/slots/base_attr_map verdict and threads the resulting setter functions into the generated script.

text: Who calls _split_what to separate filter arguments into classes, names and attributes?
rationale: Both filter factories split their arguments with it — include (src/attr/filters.py:36) and exclude (filters.py:63) — plus the direct unit test tests/test_filters.py:test_splits (34).

text: Which tests call to_bool, the boolean-string converter?
rationale: tests/test_converters.py carries the seven call sites: test_unhashable (350), the truthy table test_truthy (356-358) and the falsy table test_falsy (364-366).

text: Which tests use cmp_using to build custom comparison classes?
rationale: tests/test_cmp.py: TestDundersUnnamedClass instantiates one unnamed Comparable in a class body (307), test_eq_must_specified pins the eq-required error (346) and test_not_implemented_is_propagated checks NotImplemented flow (364).

text: Who calls set_run_validators to flip the global validator switch?
rationale: validators.set_disabled is the modern front door (src/attr/validators.py:57); the disabled context manager toggles it off and restores it (validators.py:85/89); tests/test_config.py:test_set_run_validators (23) and tests/test_setattr.py:test_validate_respects_run_validators_config (186) exercise it directly.

text: Who reads get_run_validators to check whether validators run?
rationale: validators.get_disabled negates it for the modern API (src/attr/validators.py:69), the disabled context manager snapshots the previous state through it (validators.py:84), and tests/test_config.py:test_get_run_validators (33) asserts it directly.

text: Which tests exercise the validators.disabled context manager?
rationale: tests/test_validators.py: test_disabled_ctx (83), the exception-path test_disabled_ctx_with_errors (94) and the nesting regression test_disabled_ctx_nested (107, two call sites).

text: Which test classes use instance_of as their field validator?
rationale: 63 precise call sites across the suite; the class-level fixtures are C1/C1Slots in tests/test_functional.py (27/33), ValidatedAttribute in tests/test_setattr.py (84), Validated in tests/test_next_gen.py (64) and the slots twins in tests/test_slots.py (32/56).

text: Which validator classes declare their fields with is_callable checks?

text: Where is the None-tolerant optional validator factory used inside the validators module?
rationale: The deep validator classes declare their fields with it: _DeepIterable's iterable_validator (src/attr/validators.py:336) and _DeepMapping's three validators (validators.py:389-391) use optional(is_callable()) so the slots stay None-able; optional itself is defined at validators.py:214.

text: Who calls default_if_none, the None-substituting converter factory?
rationale: _NotValidator wraps its wrapped-validator argument with it so rejected values can carry a default (src/attr/validators.py:638); the argument-validation tests live in tests/test_converters.py: test_missing_default (180), test_too_many_defaults (187), test_factory_takes_self (194), test_none_factory (221).

text: Which tests exercise deep_iterable validation?
rationale: The suite in tests/test_validators.py: test_success_member_only (504), test_success_member_and_iterable (513), test_fail_invalid_member (550), test_fail_invalid_iterable (561), test_fail_invalid_member_and_iterable (572); _NotValidator also composes one at src/attr/validators.py:644.

text: Who uses matches_re to validate regex-shaped values?
rationale: tests/test_setattr.py:ValidatedAttribute applies it to an attribute (84); the dedicated testers in tests/test_validators.py are ReTester (185), MatchTester (202) and the precompiled-pattern test test_precompiled_pattern_no_flags (227).

text: Which tests call in_ to validate membership?
rationale: tests/test_validators.py: test_success_with_value (411), test_fail (420), test_fail_with_string (438), test_repr (453), the C fixture class (464) and the composition test test_composable_with_in_pass (1209).

text: Which tests exercise not_, the negating validator?
rationale: tests/test_validators.py: test_success_because_fails (1174) and test_fails_because_success (1188) pin the polarity, while test_composable_with_matches_re_pass (1241) and test_composable_with_matches_re_fail (1252) pin the or_-composition.

text: Who calls or_ to build alternative validators?
rationale: Three call sites in tests/test_validators.py: test_success (1378), test_fail (1386) and test_repr (1395).

text: Which code paths call and_ to compose validators?
rationale: attrib auto-wraps validator lists (src/attr/_make.py:191), _CountingAttr.validator folds decorator-stacked validators (_make.py:2822), and the two deep factories flatten already-composed ones (src/attr/validators.py:381-383 and 451-455).

text: Which tests call max_len to validate bounded sequences?
rationale: Five call sites in tests/test_validators.py: the shared loop test_validators_iterables (798), the parametrized Tester class (974/997/1015) and test_repr (1024).

text: Who calls do_it, the next-gen class-building entry point?
rationale: Only the wrap closure inside define drives it — three dispatching call sites in one body (src/attr/_next_gen.py:418 for bare classes, 421/423 for used-as-decorator and used-direct forms).

text: What breaks if attrib changes how single fields are declared?
rationale: 18 precise depth-0 callers: the library-internal ones are _transform_attrs (src/attr/_make.py:417), make_class (3259), _AndValidator (3319), field (src/attr/_next_gen.py:605) and VersionInfo (src/attr/_version_info.py:33-35); the transitive closure reaches 204 symbols through the whole class-building chain.

text: What is the blast radius of changing fields, the attribute-tuple accessor?
rationale: 69 precise depth-0 callers — every helper consumes it (asdict _funcs.py:80, astuple 274, assoc 415, resolve_types 488, evolve _make.py:633, validate 1983) plus the introspection tests; the recursive closure is 79 symbols.

text: What breaks if Factory changes how default factories are stored?
rationale: 21 precise depth-0 callers (attrib _make.py:181, _CountingAttr.default 2839, default_if_none converters.py:101 and the default-heavy tests); the closure through attrib and the class builder reaches 224 symbols.

text: What breaks if _CountingAttr changes its counter or slots layout?
rationale: Exactly one production path constructs it — attrib (src/attr/_make.py:196) — but everything authored with attr.ib sits above that edge, so the precise closure still spans 205 symbols.

text: What is the blast radius of changing and_, the validator composer?
rationale: Eight precise depth-0 callers: attrib's list auto-wrap (src/attr/_make.py:191), _CountingAttr.validator's decorator stacking (2822), deep_iterable and deep_mapping flattening (src/attr/validators.py:381-383/451-455) plus the composition tests; closure 204 symbols.

text: What breaks if _transform_attrs changes how fields are collected and ordered?
rationale: Eight precise callers, all shallow: the sole production caller _ClassBuilder.__init__ (src/attr/_make.py:682) and the seven direct unit tests in tests/test_make.py (closure stops at 8 — the builder methods call it through __init__, not by name).

text: What breaks if _make_init_script changes the generated __init__ protocol?
rationale: Three precise depth-0 callers — add_init (src/attr/_make.py:1082), add_attrs_init (1118) and the parity helper tests/test_dunders.py:_add_init (89); above them the closure climbs through the builder to 33 symbols.

text: What is the blast radius of the init source emitter _attrs_to_init_script?
rationale: One precise depth-0 caller — _make_init_script (src/attr/_make.py:2038) — with the closure above it reaching 34 symbols: every path that generates an init method plus their tests.

text: What breaks if _determine_setters changes which assignment style init uses?
rationale: Exactly _attrs_to_init_script consumes its verdict (src/attr/_make.py:2184); the closure above add_init/add_attrs_init spans 35 symbols.

text: What breaks if make_class changes its class-body packing?
rationale: 55 precise depth-0 callers — the hypothesis strategies (tests/strategies.py:71/200), the shared fixture tests/utils.py:simple_class and the dedicated suite in tests/test_make.py; closure 66 symbols.

text: What is the blast radius of cmp_using, the custom-comparison factory?
rationale: Three precise callers, all tests (tests/test_cmp.py:307/346/364) — the generated comparison classes are dynamic, so nothing static sits above it (closure 3).

text: What breaks if to_bool changes which strings count as true?
rationale: Three precise callers in tests/test_converters.py (350-366) — users apply it as a converter value, not a call target, so the static closure is exactly the test suite (3).

text: What is the blast radius of default_if_none?
rationale: Seven precise depth-0 callers: _NotValidator's default wrapping (src/attr/validators.py:638) and the six argument/behavior tests in tests/test_converters.py; closure 21 symbols through the validator plumbing.

text: What breaks if _split_what changes how filter arguments are bucketed?
rationale: Both filter factories sit directly upstream — include (src/attr/filters.py:36) and exclude (63) — plus tests/test_filters.py:test_splits; the closure doubles through the factories' users to 6.

text: What is the blast radius of include, the asdict/astuple allow-filter factory?
rationale: Three precise callers (tests/test_filters.py:59/79, tests/test_validators.py:468) — filters are passed as values, so the closure is flat (3).

text: What breaks if _collect_base_attrs changes inherited-field collection?
rationale: One precise caller — _transform_attrs's collect_by_mro branch (src/attr/_make.py:452); the closure climbs through the builder to 9 symbols.

text: What is the blast radius of the wrap closure inside the attrs decorator?
rationale: Exactly one precise caller names it — attrs itself (src/attr/_make.py:1583) — but the closure through the decorator and every @attr.s class reaches 25 symbols.

text: What breaks if Converter changes how wrapped converters are called?
rationale: 14 precise depth-0 callers: the script emitter _attrs_to_init_script (src/attr/_make.py:2215), pipe (3405), optional (src/attr/converters.py:61) and the converter test suite; the closure is the dataset's largest at 251 symbols.

text: What is the blast radius of instance_of, the most-used validator factory?
rationale: 34 precise depth-0 callers (every fixture class in tests/test_functional.py, tests/test_slots.py, tests/test_setattr.py plus _NotValidator at src/attr/validators.py:646); closure 55 symbols.

text: What breaks if _default_init_alias_for changes private-argument aliasing?
rationale: Five precise depth-0 callers: _transform_attrs fills aliases before and after field_transformer (src/attr/_make.py:472/496), Attribute.evolve recomputes them (2622), Attribute.__setstate__ (2647), _CountingAttr's own slots (2727) and the test helper tests/utils.py:simple_attr; closure 213 symbols.

text: Trace the flow from applying the attr.s decorator to a finished class.
rationale: attrs (src/attr/_make.py:1325) validates its options, its wrap closure (1441) computes the ClassProps and enters _ClassBuilder.__init__ (674), which runs _transform_attrs (682) to collect fields; build_class (796) then finalizes slots or patches the original class.

text: Trace the flow of generating a class's __init__ method.
rationale: add_init (src/attr/_make.py:1081) gathers the builder state and calls _make_init_script (1997), which filters init-taking fields and delegates the source emission to _attrs_to_init_script (2038); that emitter asks _determine_setters (2107) how assignments must be made and threads _setattr (2066) or plain assignment into the script.

text: Trace the flow of creating a slotted class.
rationale: build_class routes slots=True into _create_slots_class (src/attr/_make.py:857): it strips field names from the class dict, collects inherited slots, appends the hash-cache slot when caching, and rebuilds the class with type(); pickling support comes from _make_getstate_setstate (1021).

text: Trace the flow of finalizing a non-slotted attrs class.
rationale: build_class's else branch (src/attr/_make.py:807) calls _patch_original_class (821): the accumulated _cls_dict dunders are setattr'd onto the original class, leftover attr.ib class attributes are deleted, and an inherited attrs __setattr__ is reset to object's when not overridden.

text: Trace the flow of generating a class's __hash__ method.
rationale: add_hash (src/attr/_make.py:1066) asks _make_hash_script (1611) for the source: it filters hashable fields, seeds a type_hash from _generate_unique_filename, and append_hash_computation_lines (1638) emits the tuple lines — wrapped in a _CacheHashWrapper branch when cache_hash is on; the runtime twin _add_hash (1683) attaches the same script to Factory/Converter/_CountingAttr.

text: Trace the flow of generating a class's __eq__ method.
rationale: add_eq (src/attr/_make.py:1142) calls _make_eq_script (1709), which emits the identity guard plus one and-chained comparison per eq field (honoring eq_key) and attaches the module-level __ne__ (1697) beside it; the import-time twin _add_eq (1802) does the same for Factory/Converter/_CountingAttr.

text: Trace the flow of generating ordering methods for a class.
rationale: add_order (src/attr/_make.py:1156) pulls four methods from _make_order (1746), whose inner attrs_to_tuple (1752) applies per-field order_key functions; the generated __lt__ (1763) and siblings compare those tuples after the same-class guard.

text: Trace the flow of generating a class's __repr__ method.
rationale: add_repr (src/attr/_make.py:1000) requests the script from _make_repr_script (1819) and queues _attach_repr for the build; the import-time twin _add_repr (1876) attaches the same generated repr to Factory/Converter/_CountingAttr (see the _CountingAttr re-wrap at _make.py:2844).

text: Trace the recursion when asdict serializes nested attrs instances.
rationale: asdict (src/attr/_funcs.py:28) walks fields() and, per value, branches on _ATOMIC_TYPES, has(value_type) for nested attrs classes (recursing at 95), and collections/dicts whose elements go through _asdict_anything (154) — which itself recurses back into asdict for nested attrs values (172).

text: Trace the recursion when astuple serializes nested attrs instances.
rationale: astuple (src/attr/_funcs.py:232) walks fields(), keeps atomic values, recurses into has(value_type) members (287) and maps element-wise recursion across collections and dict items (299-341), ending in the caller's tuple_factory (351).

text: Trace the flow of evolve creating a modified copy of an instance.
rationale: evolve (src/attr/_make.py:587) unpacks the single positional instance, reads fields(cls) (633), fills every init-taking field's init alias from the current instance unless overridden (634-640), and finally calls cls(**changes) with the merged keyword arguments.

text: Trace the flow of make_class building a class from names.
rationale: make_class (src/attr/_make.py:3206) NFKC-normalizes the name, packs a list of names into attrib() defaults (3259), pops pre/post-init and user __init__ into a fresh class body, resolves cmp into eq/order via _determine_attrs_eq_order (3294), and finally runs the attrs decorator with these= (3301).

text: Trace the flow of comparing a VersionInfo against a plain tuple.
rationale: __eq__ (src/attr/_version_info.py:70) delegates the shape negotiation to _ensure_tuple (51): same-class others are converted with astuple (60), non-tuples or wrong-length tuples raise NotImplementedError (caught as NotImplemented), and the truncated self-tuple is compared element-wise.

text: Trace the flow of reading attr.__version_info__ at runtime.
rationale: The package's module-level __getattr__ (src/attr/__init__.py:87, built by _make_getattr at 81) intercepts the attribute, loads importlib metadata, and parses the version string through VersionInfo._from_version_string (src/attr/_version_info.py:39) into a VersionInfo instance.

text: Trace the flow of optional copying type hints from the wrapped converter.
rationale: optional (src/attr/converters.py:21) picks the Converter-aware or plain closure shape, then _AnnotationExtractor (src/attr/_compat.py:40) introspects the wrapped callable's signature — get_first_param_type (54) feeds the val annotation (converters.py:52-54) and get_return_type (67) the return annotation — before optional returns the bare closure or a Converter (61).

text: Trace the flow of the validators.disabled context manager.
rationale: disabled (src/attr/validators.py:73) snapshots the current state via get_run_validators (84), turns validators off with set_run_validators(False) (85), yields, and restores the snapshot in the finally block (89) — the nestability fix in 26.1.0 rides this snapshot/restore pairing.

text: Trace the flow of building a deep_iterable validator from its arguments.
rationale: deep_iterable (src/attr/validators.py:361) folds list/tuple member or iterable validators through and_ (380-383) and returns _DeepIterable (384), whose fields were themselves validated with optional(is_callable()) at class-definition time (334-337).

text: Trace what happens when assigning to an attribute of a define() class with default hooks.
rationale: define's default on_setattr is _DEFAULT_ON_SETATTR = setters.pipe(setters.convert, setters.validate) (src/attr/_make.py:59); add_setattr emits a __setattr__ (1182-1193) that looks the field up in sa_attrs, runs the hook, then object.__setattr__ — the pipe's wrapped_pipe folds convert (src/attr/setters.py:56) then validate (38) over the new value.

text: Trace the pickle round-trip of a slotted attrs class.
rationale: _make_getstate_setstate (src/attr/_make.py:1021) builds the pair: slots_getstate (1030) reads every field by name into a dict, and slots_setstate (1038) restores via bound object.__setattr__ — accepting both the pre-22.2.0 tuple shape and the current dict, and re-initializing the hash-cache slot to None when cache_hash is on.

text: Trace the flow inside _transform_attrs from counting attributes to the field tuple.
rationale: _transform_attrs (src/attr/_make.py:379) gathers own _CountingAttrs (or annotation-driven ones), converts each through Attribute.from_counting_attr (439), merges inherited fields via _collect_base_attrs (452), fills missing aliases with _default_init_alias_for (472/496), applies the field_transformer, and packs the result with _make_attr_tuple_class (502).

text: Trace how a Converter ends up called with the right arguments in generated init code.
rationale: Converter.__init__ (src/attr/_make.py:3117) introspects the wrapped callable via _AnnotationExtractor (3122) and binds the matching __call__ lambda; when _attrs_to_init_script emits assignments, _fmt_converter_call (3150) renders the global-name call with the correct self/field arguments, which _setattr_with_converter (2073) embeds in the generated setter line.

text: Trace stacking a second validator on a field via the attr.validators decorator.
rationale: _CountingAttr.validator (src/attr/_make.py:2811) returns the decorated method unchanged but stores it — folding an existing validator through and_ (2822); its sibling default (2825) raises DefaultAlreadySetError if a default exists and otherwise wraps the method in Factory(meth, takes_self=True).

text: Where is the method that replaces a URL's scheme defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:1153 defines URL.with_scheme: it lowercases the scheme, rejects non-str with TypeError, refuses scheme replacement on relative URLs for host-requiring schemes (SCHEME_REQUIRES_HOST, 1160-1165), and rebuilds via from_parts keeping path/query/fragment.

text: Where is the accessor that reduces a URL to scheme, host and port defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:695 defines URL.origin, a thin wrapper over the cached_property _origin (709) which strips user/password/path/query/fragment — rebuilding a bare netloc through host_subcomponent and make_netloc when credentials were present.

text: Where is the method that strips scheme and authority, keeping only the relative reference defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:725 defines URL.relative: it raises ValueError for non-absolute URLs (731-732) and returns from_parts("", "", path, query, fragment).

text: Where is the operator that appends a path segment with the slash operator defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:628 defines URL.__truediv__ (url / 'segment'): non-str operands return NotImplemented, str operands delegate to _make_child((str(name),)).

text: Where is the modulo operator on URL, the one that merges query parameters, defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:633 defines URL.__mod__ (url % query) as a one-line alias delegating to update_query.

text: Where is the method that replaces a URL's path defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:1251 defines URL.with_path: unencoded inputs are PATH_QUOTER-quoted and dot-normalized when a netloc exists (1262-1264), a leading slash is forced, keep_query/keep_fragment flags preserve the other components, and the result is rebuilt with from_parts.

text: Where is the property that renders path and query together, decoded, defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:1004 defines the cached_property path_qs: it returns the decoded path, or f"{self.path}?{self.query_string}" when a query exists (1006); the raw-encoded twin raw_path_qs sits at 1009.

text: Where is the property that exposes parsed query parameters as a multidict defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:976 defines the cached_property URL.query returning MultiDictProxy(MultiDict(self._parsed_query)); _parsed_query (971) is the parser that turns the raw query string into pairs via query_to_pairs.

text: Where is the NFKC safety check that rejects netlocs confusable with authority delimiters defined?
rationale: yarl/_parse.py:108 defines _check_netloc, adapted from urllib.parse._checknetloc: it strips @ : # ? before unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', ...) and raises ValueError when a delimiter character appears only after normalization (the \u2100 'a/c' SSRF trick); split_url calls it for non-ASCII netlocs (_parse.py:103-104).

text: Where is the singleton enum used for unset values in yarl's caching API defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:151 defines UndefinedType, a single-variant Enum whose _singleton instance becomes the module-level UNDEFINED sentinel at _url.py:157 — the marker cache_configure uses to mean 'leave this cache alone'.

text: Where is the TypedDict describing the host-encoding cache statistics defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:160 defines CacheInfo with one _CacheInfo slot per lru_cache — idna_encode, idna_decode, ip_address, host_validate and encode_host — the shape cache_info() reports.

text: Where is the TypedDict that enumerates every per-instance cached URL component defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:170 defines _InternalURLCache (total=False): from _val and _origin through parts, name, suffixes — the declared key set of URL._cache.

text: Where is the property that returns the host with IPv6 brackets restored defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:858 defines the cached_property host_subcomponent: None for relative URLs, otherwise the raw host wrapped in brackets whenever it contains a colon (IPv6 literals, 877); host_port_subcomponent (880) builds on it for Host headers.

text: Where is the path variant that keeps encoded slashes and percent signs intact defined?
rationale: yarl/_url.py:958 defines the cached_property path_safe: same '/'-for-absolute defaulting as path (949) but decoded with PATH_SAFE_UNQUOTER, which leaves %2F and %25 encoded.

text: Which tests exercise URL.origin?
rationale: The origin suite in tests/test_url.py: test_origin (76), test_origin_is_equal_to_self (81), test_origin_with_no_auth (86), test_origin_nonascii (91), test_origin_ipv6 (96), test_origin_not_absolute_url (102), test_origin_no_scheme (108), plus the zone-mutation regression test_ipv6_zone_rfc6874_mutation_apis (631).

text: Which tests call URL.relative?
rationale: tests/test_url.py carries test_relative (2553), test_relative_is_relative (2559), test_relative_abs_parts_are_removed (2566) and test_relative_fails_on_rel_url (2576); tests/test_url_parsing.py adds the scheme-colon regression test_relative_keeps_colon_after_slash (934).

text: Which tests exercise URL.with_scheme?
rationale: tests/test_url_update_netloc.py: test_with_scheme (10), test_with_scheme_uppercased (15), test_with_scheme_for_relative_url (34), test_with_scheme_for_relative_file_url (40), test_with_scheme_invalid_type (46) and the port-normalization matrix test_with_default_port_normalization (275-277).

text: Which tests exercise URL.with_path?
rationale: The dedicated matrix in tests/test_url.py: test_with_path (1486), test_with_path_nonascii (1494), test_with_path_percent_encoded (1502), test_with_path_encoded (1510), test_with_path_dots (1534), test_with_path_keep_query_keep_fragment_flags (1589).

text: Who calls _make_child to append path segments?
rationale: Exactly the two segment-appending APIs: __truediv__ for the single-segment slash operator (yarl/_url.py:631) and joinpath for the multi-segment API (1559).

text: Which query-mutating methods rebuild their result through from_parts_uncached?
rationale: The three query mutators each end in it: with_query (yarl/_url.py:1292), extend_query (1320) and update_query (1388).

text: Who calls build_pre_encoded_url, the already-encoded builder?
rationale: Exactly one precise caller: URL.build's encoded=True branch (yarl/_url.py:509).

text: Who calls _check_netloc during URL parsing?
rationale: Exactly one precise caller: split_url invokes it when a non-ASCII netloc is present (yarl/_parse.py:103-104), before returning the five components.

text: Which tests drive cache_configure, the lru-cache sizing API?
rationale: tests/test_cache.py: teardown_module resets state (9), test_cache_configure_default (28), test_cache_configure_None (32), test_cache_configure_explicit (73) and the deprecation-warning pair test_cache_configure_waring (90/99).

text: Which tests exercise URL.joinpath?
rationale: The joinpath suite in tests/test_url.py: test_joinpath (1309), test_joinpath_empty_segments (1342), test_joinpath_backtrack_to_base (1349), test_joinpath_single_empty_segments (1359), test_joinpath_relative (1378), test_joinpath_encoding (1425), test_joinpath_edgecases (1440) and the forbidden-leading-slash regression test_joinpath_path_starting_from_slash_is_forbidden (1449).

text: Which tests call URL.with_user?
rationale: tests/test_url_update_netloc.py: test_with_user (51), test_with_user_non_ascii (56), test_with_user_percent_encoded (65), test_with_user_for_relative_url (74), test_with_user_invalid_type (80), test_with_user_None (85); the RFC 6874 regression test_ipv6_zone_rfc6874_mutation_apis sits in tests/test_url.py (633).

text: Which tests exercise URL.with_port?
rationale: tests/test_url_update_netloc.py: test_with_port (270) and the normalization matrix test_with_default_port_normalization (276-277), test_with_custom_port_normalization (282-284), test_with_explicit_port_normalization (290); tests/test_url.py contributes test_ipv6_zone_rfc6874_mutation_apis (632).

text: What breaks if _make_child changes how path segments are appended?
rationale: The two segment-appending APIs sit directly upstream — __truediv__ (yarl/_url.py:631) and joinpath (1559); above them the closure spans 15 symbols including their test suites and the slash-operator regressions.

text: What is the blast radius of build_pre_encoded_url?
rationale: One precise depth-0 caller — URL.build's encoded=True branch (yarl/_url.py:509) — but above it the closure reaches 70 symbols: every builder test and the DEFAULT_PORTS normalization matrix.

text: What breaks if _check_netloc loosens its NFKC delimiter check?
rationale: Exactly split_url calls it for non-ASCII netlocs (yarl/_parse.py:103-104); through the two cached constructors and URL.__new__ the closure reaches 83 symbols — every parsed-URL path plus the SSRF-confusion tests.

text: What is the blast radius of _cache_netloc?
rationale: Four precise depth-0 callers, all raw netloc accessors on cache miss: raw_user (yarl/_url.py:784), raw_password (805), raw_host (830) and explicit_port (936); each is a cached_property leaf, so the closure stays at 4.

text: What breaks if split_netloc changes its authority decomposition?
rationale: Three precise depth-0 callers: encode_url for complex netlocs (yarl/_url.py:236), URL.build with an authority= argument (525) and _cache_netloc (664); the closure through the constructors is 87 symbols.

text: What is the blast radius of _encode_relative_scheme_colon?
rationale: Five precise depth-0 callers — every constructor/render path that can emit a scheme-less path: encode_url (270), build_pre_encoded_url (328), from_parts_uncached (344), build (552) and human_repr (1571); closure 93 symbols.

text: What breaks if encode_url changes how unencoded strings are parsed and quoted?
rationale: Only URL.__new__ calls it (twice — the str and subclass branches, yarl/_url.py:445/453), but the closure above the constructor reaches 81 symbols across the package and tests.

text: What is the blast radius of pre_encoded_url?
rationale: Only URL.__new__ calls it (yarl/_url.py:445/453, the encoded=True branch); like its twin encode_url the closure above spans 81 symbols.

text: What breaks if joinpath changes its segment-joining rules?
rationale: Thirteen precise depth-0 callers, all tests — the joinpath suite in tests/test_url.py (1309-1449) plus benchmark helpers; the closure is flat at 13 because the API is a leaf.

text: What is the blast radius of with_path?
rationale: Fifteen precise depth-0 callers: the with_path matrix in tests/test_url.py (1486-1589) and the benchmark helpers; a leaf API, so the closure stays at 15.

text: What breaks if origin changes what it strips?
rationale: Nine precise depth-0 callers, all in the test surface: the origin suite in tests/test_url.py (76-108, 631) and benchmark helpers; closure 9.

text: What is the blast radius of with_scheme?
rationale: Nine precise depth-0 callers: the with_scheme tests in tests/test_url_update_netloc.py (10-46) and the port-normalization matrix (275-293) that pins scheme/port interaction; closure 9.

text: Trace the flow of appending one path segment with the slash operator.
rationale: __truediv__ (yarl/_url.py:628) rejects non-str operands with NotImplemented and delegates to _make_child (1109), which quotes the segment with PATH_QUOTER, rejects leading slashes, and resolves dot segments through normalize_path_segments (1147) before from_parts rebuilds the URL.

text: Trace the flow of url % query merging parameters into the query string.
rationale: __mod__ (yarl/_url.py:633) is an alias for update_query, which serializes the argument through get_str_query (yarl/_query.py:85) and rebuilds the URL via from_parts_uncached (yarl/_url.py:1388) keeping the other components.

text: Trace the flow of replacing a URL's scheme.
rationale: with_scheme (yarl/_url.py:1153) type-checks and lowercases the scheme, guards relative URLs against host-requiring schemes via SCHEME_REQUIRES_HOST (1160-1165), and rebuilds through the lru-cached from_parts (the from_parts_uncached constructor at 336) keeping netloc/path/query/fragment.

text: Trace the flow of computing a URL's origin when credentials are present.
rationale: origin (yarl/_url.py:695) delegates to the cached _origin (709): a netloc containing '@' triggers host_subcomponent (719) to re-extract the encoded host and make_netloc (720) to rebuild a bare authority before from_parts assembles scheme+netloc only; URLs that are already bare return self (722).

text: Trace the flow of dropping scheme and authority from a URL.
rationale: relative (yarl/_url.py:725) requires a netloc (ValueError otherwise) and calls the lru-cached from_parts (from_parts_uncached at 336) with empty scheme and netloc, keeping path, query and fragment untouched.

text: Trace the flow of reading url.query for the first time.
rationale: The cached_property query (yarl/_url.py:976) wraps _parsed_query (971) in MultiDictProxy(MultiDict(...)); _parsed_query parses the raw encoded query string through query_to_pairs (yarl/_parse.py:221) and caches the pair list in the instance cache.

text: Trace the flow of converting a URL to bytes.
rationale: __bytes__ (yarl/_url.py:583) is defined as str(self).encode('ascii') on top of __str__ (564), which applies default-port normalization and renders the five components through unsplit_result (yarl/_parse.py:171).

text: Trace the flow of reconfiguring yarl's caches via cache_configure.
rationale: cache_configure (yarl/_url.py:1752) maps the deprecated ip_address_size/host_validate_size arguments onto encode_host_size with a DeprecationWarning, then re-wraps the unwrapped functions in fresh lru_cache instances: _encode_host, _idna_decode and _idna_encode (global rebinding at the tail of the function); cache_info (1740) reports their sizes through the CacheInfo TypedDict and cache_clear (1732) empties them.

text: Trace the flow of replacing a URL's user credential.
rationale: with_user (yarl/_url.py:1168) quotes the new user with QUOTER, keeps or clears the password (None clears both), rejects relative URLs, re-extracts the host through host_subcomponent (1186), reassembles the authority with make_netloc (1187) and rebuilds via the lru-cached from_parts keeping path/query/fragment.

text: Trace the flow of dropping selected query parameters from a URL.
rationale: without_query_params (yarl/_url.py:1392) intersects the requested names with self.query keys (returning self unchanged when nothing matches), then re-serializes the surviving query.items() pairs as a tuple through with_query (1401), which routes them into get_str_query and from_parts_uncached.
